basis: Congenital dislocations, joint hypermobility, hyperextensible skin and impaired wound healing define this EDS subtype.
Congenital cardiac malformations are common, including AV canal defects in 7/21. Visceral malposition alone does not establish organ damage.
Isolated hypotrichosis affects scalp and body hair, eyebrows and eyelashes; eyelashes are hair rather than intrinsic eye disease.
Congenital skin absence defines ACC; supplied HPO reports calvarial defects and spinal dysraphism at 80-99%, supporting skeletal and neural involvement.
Defined skeletal myopathy with abnormal muscle mitochondria; no supplied evidence establishes a specific metabolic disorder or other organ damage.
Intestinal dysfunction and impaired stool control are explicitly caused by damage or developmental defects of bowel innervation.
Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define Carpenter syndrome; developmental impairment is common. Cardiac, ocular and hearing damage lack clear >=30% support.
Autoimmune scleroderma lung disease; skin fibrosis affects >90% and gastrointestinal fibrosis/dysmotility about 80-90% in systemic sclerosis.
Disorder of cardiac impulse generation or conduction; no additional organ damage applies across this umbrella.
Transferred maternal autoantibodies impair neuromuscular junction function. Feeding and respiratory weakness do not establish separate gut or lung damage.
Epilepsy with developmental impairment defines a brain and neurodevelopmental disorder.
Inherited congenital lens opacity; no additional organ involvement is established.
Disturbed nutrient intake or utilization defines a nutritional/metabolic disorder; no specific damaged organ is common across the umbrella.
Renal cystic disease; mitral regurgitation occurs in 51/163 (~31%), supporting valve involvement. Common hepatic cysts usually preserve liver function.
Inherited porphyrin metabolism disorder with acute neurovisceral attacks; pain alone is not gut damage, and neuropathic damage is not established at >=30%.
Paralysis causes loss of laryngeal adductor motor function, affecting the upper airway and its neuromotor control.
Intellectual disability and spastic quadriparesis define central nervous system dysfunction; spasticity alone does not establish primary muscle disease.
Congenital microcephaly, skeletal growth restriction and limb malformations define this developmental spectrum.
GATA2 deficiency affects immune and marrow cell production. Lung failure is variable; myeloid malignancies are separately diagnosed outcomes.
Molar tooth malformation and developmental delay occur in 4/4. Individual ocular findings occur in 1/4 and do not establish common intrinsic eye damage.
Aspirated meconium directly injures and obstructs neonatal lungs. Pulmonary hypertension and neurologic injury are minority complications.
Chronic inflammation of the tympanic membrane; the concept does not establish a specific infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Premature fusion of both lambdoid skull sutures is a skeletal malformation; neurologic damage is not intrinsic to the diagnosis.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the heart or blood vessels; no other organ involvement is common across this cancer umbrella.
Inherited glomerular disease with nephrotic syndrome, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and kidney failure; stage 5 CKD occurs in 3/3.
